property_summary: For any caller and any pre-funded balance, a successful withdraw() must pay the contract's entire balance to c.Owner() (reverting otherwise) and leave c with zero balance; the mutant deviates by sending funds to msg.sender instead of the recorded Owner.

For any caller, withdraw() may only succeed when the caller is the recorded Owner, and then the contract's entire balance must be transferred to c.Owner() (leaving c with zero balance); the mutant pays the funds to msg.sender instead of the recorded Owner, so in a scenario where the recorded Owner differs from the executing caller the funds end up with the wrong party.

For any owner/deployer and any caller, withdraw() must succeed only for c.Owner() and must pay c's entire balance to c.Owner() (visible as c.Owner()'s EOA balance rising by exactly c's prior balance while c drops to 0 and every other party gains nothing); the mutant pays the caller instead of the recorded Owner, so when the executing caller differs from the recorded Owner the funds are misdirected.

For any caller who is the recorded Owner and any funded balance, a successful withdraw() transfers c's entire balance to c.Owner() and leaves address(c).balance == 0; the mutant redirects funds to msg.sender, so whenever the executing caller differs from the recorded Owner the payout target (and the resulting balance changes) deviate from the rule.
Only the Owner may move funds out of C via Command, so a non-owner's Command call must revert and leave the target unchanged.
